reply_text:
I found one dated prediction from 2016, in a Bloomberg Businessweek question-and-answer interview. Hassabis said full AI (artificial general intelligence, which the question asked about) was "many decades away." He added that he'd be "surprised if it took more than, let's say, 100 years."

- **Where it ran:** the Businessweek Interview Issue dated August 8–21, 2016. The interview is printed as "condensed and edited," so the words are his as Bloomberg published them.
- **The Verge interview did not open.** Sam Byford's March 2016 interview with Hassabis during the AlphaGo match against Lee Sedol (the Go world champion) was refused by the page fetcher. I'm quoting nothing from it. I did read a Japanese site's translation of the same interview (Gigazine). Its answers on AI-assisted science, CERN and home robots name no dates. The only time span in it is DeepMind's two-to-three-year research cycle, which describes how the lab works rather than predicting anything.
- **Nothing else qualified.** A Medill student report on his February 2016 talk at the AAAS conference has him saying AlphaGo came "a decade earlier than most experts in the field were predicting." That looks backward, so it isn't a prediction. A 2016 PCGamesN profile of him has no dated forecasts.
- **Not checked:** his April 2016 talk at MIT's Center for Brains, Minds and Machines (CBMM) is a video and I didn't open it. It may be worth checking by hand.
